author: Han Li
description:
US President Donald Trump’s nominee to lead the United States’ international broadcasting agency pledged on Thursday to sharpen its media challenge to China, including by expanding into short-form videos, podcasts and diaspora group chats.
Sarah B. Rogers told a Senate committee hearing that Asia would remain a top regional priority for the US Agency for Global Media (USAGM), which oversees Voice of America (VOA) and funds Radio Free Asia and other international broadcasters.
“China is rapacious...
title: Trump nominee vows to sharpen US media challenge to China

author: Liu Zhen
description:
As the People’s Liberation Army marks its 99th anniversary on August 1, one year from the deadline for its centenary goals, its evolution highlights the past, present and future of China’s military strategy. In the first part of a series, Liu Zhen examines how the PLA’s strategies have developed from guerrilla warfare to hi-tech conflict.
In April 1932, Xi Zhongxun, 18, led the newly formed Fifth Detachment of the Red Army’s Shaanxi-Gansu Guerrilla Force marching in the mountains in Yongshou...
title: The PLA at 99: how China’s military went from ragtag rifles to world-class force

author: Zhou Xiaoming
description:
A scaremongering narrative has taken root in Western corridors and financial press columns: China, having saturated developed markets, is now aiming to crush fragile industries in developing nations, effectively slamming the door on their industrial dreams. It is a convenient little tale. However, it does not hold up against empirical evidence.
The premise assumes that China and the Global South are fighting over the same slice of the global consumption pie – cheap T-shirts, plastic sandals,...
title: China’s exports feed the Global South’s industrial engines

author: Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
The United States sanctioned two China-based companies and a Chinese executive on Thursday over their alleged support for Iran’s Mahan Air, which Washington described as the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ “airline of choice” for transporting weapons, military personnel and equipment.
The action marked the second consecutive day that Washington targeted mainland China- or Hong Kong-linked businesses accused of supporting Tehran, broadening its latest pressure campaign from Iranian oil...
title: US sanctions Mahan Air’s China network over alleged support for Iran’s IRGC

author: Lucy Quaggin
description:
The United Nations Security Council began the selection process for the next secretary general on Thursday, with a first “straw poll” held behind closed doors to evaluate support for candidates vying for the role at the embattled world body.
Antonio Guterres, the current UN chief, is set to complete his second five-year term on the final day of 2026, leaving the high-profile role open for a new leader whose first day would be January 1, 2027.
The 15-member Security Council is responsible for...
title: Selection for next UN chief gets underway with first ‘straw poll’

author: Nayan Seth
description:
China on Thursday voiced “serious concern” over recent US economic restrictions during a video call between Vice-Premier He Lifeng, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer.
The exchange took place as both sides sought to finalise economic deliverables ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s expected visit to the United States in September.
“The Chinese side expressed serious concern over the recent economic and trade restrictions imposed by the United...
title: China voices ‘serious concern’ over new US curbs in senior trade talks

author: Ling Xin
description:
Researchers based in China or having a Chinese surname were far less likely than their US and Canadian counterparts to have papers published in the world’s most prestigious journals, according to a new study.
Just 2.5 per cent of submissions from China-based researchers were accepted, compared with 8.3 per cent overall for those from North America, a team found after analysing a rare dataset of more than 110,000 manuscripts submitted to Science and Science Advances between 2015 and 2020.
Even...
title: Top US science journals more likely to reject paper by Chinese authors: study

author: Liu Zhen
description:
The United States could be developing underground warfare powers and China should guard against the potential threat to its national security, Chinese think tanks have warned.
As drones and precision-guided weapons increasingly dominate ground combat in conflicts, military theorists are exploring the strategic potential of subterranean space as a possible dimension of future warfare.
Palmer Luckey, founder of defence technology company Anduril, has promoted the concept of a “subterrene” – a...
title: Could US subterranean warfare be a future threat to China’s military defences?

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Fresh images and footage have emerged of what some observers say may be a fifth prototype of China’s J-36 sixth-generation combat aircraft.
If authentic, the images offer new clues about a rapidly evolving design as Beijing races for air superiority in future warfare against rivals such as the United States.
The latest footage, circulating since earlier this month, appears to show further changes to the aircraft’s nose, air intakes, engine nozzles and landing gear. This suggests its developer,...
title: New images point to fifth prototype for China’s J-36 fighter jet in air power race with US

author: Djoomart Otorbaev
description:
Over the past 10 years, Washington, Brussels and London have made decreasing economic reliance on China a strategic goal. Western economic plans now stress supply-chain resilience, industrial sovereignty, technological leadership and national security.
The Covid-19 pandemic highlighted weaknesses in global supply networks. Increasing geostrategic tensions, export restrictions and technological rivalry have supported political backing for reshoring and “friendshoring” manufacturing.
The objective...
title: Can the West really decouple from China?

author: Shi Jiangtao
description:
Beijing accused Manila of “flagrantly infringing” on Chinese sovereignty and undermining regional peace after the Philippines formally presented its bid to the United Nations this week for extended seabed rights in the South China Sea.
The rebuttal, issued by China’s mission to the UN on Thursday, followed Manila’s presentation before the Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf (CLCS) on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Beijing said the filing violated its sovereignty, sovereign rights and...
title: China accuses Manila of ‘flagrantly infringing’ on sovereignty in UN seabed claim

author: Alcott Wei,Amber Wang
description:
Zhou Bo is a retired senior colonel in the People’s Liberation Army, a senior fellow at Tsinghua University’s Centre for International Security and Strategy, and the author of the book Should the World Fear China?
SCMP Plus readers get early access to articles in the Open Questions series.
The People’s Liberation Army (PLA) is approaching its 2027 centenary, a major benchmark set by Beijing to achieve military modernisation. What is that goal actually about?
China has set two major military...
title: Ex-PLA colonel on US’ decline and China’s nuclear arsenal

author: Victoria Bela
description:
A Chinese-led team has analysed a 240 million-year-old fossil with the oldest known preserved stomach, liver and intestinal soft tissue in reptiles.
The complete skeleton fossil has highly specialised body features that indicate it lived in the water, suggesting the marine colonisation of archosaurs was earlier and more extensive than previously believed.
The fossil of the Austronaga minuta from the Early Triassic period also offers a “unique opportunity” to study how Triassic reptiles made the...
title: Triassic fish for lunch? Chinese fossil reveals oldest preserved reptile stomach

author: William Zheng
description:
China’s top leaders will gather in Beijing in October for their most important meeting ahead of next year’s Communist Party congress, when a major reshuffle is expected and Xi Jinping is due to begin a fourth term as leader.
After a meeting of the Politburo on Thursday, the nation’s top decision-making body said the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee would be held in October, state news agency Xinhua reported.
More than 370 full and alternate members of the Central Committee –...
title: China says key plenum will be held in October

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
A parliamentary clash in Wellington has elicited a subtle rebuke from Beijing after New Zealand’s Foreign Minister Winston Peters told a Chinese-born opposition lawmaker to “go back to your own country”.
The comments on Wednesday prompted a rare social media response from Beijing’s envoy in Wellington, adding an international dimension to an already contentious domestic debate over governance and race relations in the South Pacific nation.
The controversy erupted during a parliamentary debate on...
title: China envoy makes a rare response after NZ foreign minister’s ‘go back’ slur

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
US President Donald Trump said he would be “quite disappointed” if his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping broke a personal promise not to arm Iran, even as he revived his accusation that long-time US health official Anthony Fauci helped shield Beijing from scrutiny over the origins of Covid-19.
The comments came as Fauci, who led the US response to the pandemic, appeared before a Senate committee.
Separately, Reuters has reported that Iran is expected to receive 300 to 400 Chinese-made...
title: ‘Quite disappointed’? Trump’s mixed signals ahead of Xi’s September trip

author: Fan Chen
description:
Members of a delegation from the Japanese prefecture of Okinawa paid tribute to their ancestors at the historic Ryukyu Kingdom cemetery in Beijing, highlighting a legacy of ties that China is increasingly leveraging as a counterweight in its frictions with Tokyo.
During the visit in June – first made public by the Global Times on Sunday – about a dozen delegates travelled to the site southeast of Beijing, which honours six centuries of ties between China and the former island nation later...
title: Why did an Okinawan delegation visit a Beijing cemetery amid China-Japan tensions?
